transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I’m here because... it's dispatch, mostly. And compliance. They’ve been tracking my route changes through the computer system, and making these little comments on the radio. Which, by the way, the radio in my cab has had this awful static lately. I told the maintenance guy about it last Tuesday. Or maybe Wednesday? No, it was Tuesday, because it was raining and I had to wear my yellow boots. I got those boots on sale at that shoe place off Route 9, the one right next to the diner. They make a really good cherry pie there, actually. 

But anyway, even when people say it’s just normal oversight from management, I can tell certain drivers are reporting on me. Like Dave. Dave always parks way too close to the loading dock anyway, I don't even know how he keeps his job. Did you have trouble with the parking lot here today? The spaces are just so narrow.
Do you really believe that certain drivers are reporting on you?

Well, yeah, I do. Because I know compliance is tracking my route changes through the computer system. They watch every single turn I make. Which, honestly, the computer screens in those cabs are so outdated anyway. The glare is just terrible when the sun hits it around 3 PM, right when I'm usually on the westbound interstate. I try to pull the sun visor down to see the screen better, but the hinge on mine is busted. I tried fixing it with duct tape last month, but the heat just melts the adhesive and makes it all sticky. It gets incredibly hot in there during the summer, you wouldn't believe it. 

But anyway, even when management or whoever tries to tell me it’s just normal oversight, I know it's not. I hear those little comments on the radio. Dave and the others are absolutely reporting on me to dispatch.
Do you think people are out to harm you or interfere with your work on purpose?

Harm me? I mean, I don't know if they want to physically hurt me, but interfere? Yes, absolutely on purpose. Like I was just saying, dispatch and compliance are tracking my route changes through the computer system specifically to mess with me. And the other drivers are definitely reporting on me to them, I know they are. I hear those little comments on the radio. It’s totally on purpose to ruin my routes. 

Which, honestly, my routes are hard enough right now because of all the construction on the interstate. I swear they’ve been fixing that same stretch of highway since 2019. The orange cones are just everywhere. I actually ran over one of those cones a few years ago when I was driving a smaller rig. It got completely wedged under the wheel well and made this awful scraping sound for like two miles. I had to pull over at this little gas station to yank it out, and I got grease all over my favorite jacket. It was a denim jacket, the kind with the fleece lining? My sister got it for me for my birthday. She lives in Ohio now, actually. She just got a new dog, a golden retriever mix. They are such high-energy dogs, I really don't know how she keeps up with it, especially with her working full time.
Do you think most people are generally trustworthy?

Trustworthy? I mean... mostly no. People say one thing and do another. Like dispatch, saying it's just oversight when I know they're tracking me. It's hard to trust anyone when that's going on. Which actually reminds me, my sister was saying the same thing about her new neighbors in Ohio. They smiled and waved when she moved in, but then they complained to the HOA about her trash cans being out too long. She was so mad. She had to pay a fine and everything. It was like fifty dollars, which isn't a lot, but it's the principle of it, you know? She used that money she would have spent on groceries to pay it, and then she had to eat ramen for like three days. I haven't had ramen since college. I used to put an egg in mine to make it fancy. Do you like ramen? The sodium is probably terrible for you, but it's so cheap.
Do you think your sister's experience with her neighbors is typical of how most people behave?

Typical? I don't really know. I guess maybe it is. People can be pretty two-faced, you know? But I haven't actually been out to Ohio to see her new place yet, so I haven't met them to say for sure. I was supposed to go out there for Thanksgiving, but getting time off right now is basically impossible with the schedule dispatch keeps putting me on. 

Plus, driving my own personal car that far just sounds exhausting after being in the rig all week. My car actually needs an oil change anyway. I usually take it to this little shop down on 4th street, but they raised their prices again. It used to be like thirty-five bucks and now it's almost sixty. And they always try to upsell you on the cabin air filters. I know how to change my own air filter, you literally just squeeze the sides of the glove box and pull it down. My dad taught me how to do that when I got my first car. It was this old silver Honda. The AC was completely busted, which was just miserable in July. We used to drive it out to the lake on the weekends, and we'd have to roll all the windows down, but the wind would just whip through and mess up my hair so bad. I had really long hair back then, down past my shoulders.
Do you really think dispatch and the other drivers are out to get you specifically?

Yes, specifically me. I mean, I'm here talking to you because dispatch and compliance are tracking my route changes through the computer system. They say it's just normal oversight, but I know it's not. I can hear the little comments on the radio, and I can tell certain drivers are reporting on me. It's just so obvious. 

Which, speaking of the radio, mine has been getting this awful static lately whenever I drive past the old water tower on Route 9. It’s like this loud crackling noise that just pierces right through your ears. I tried adjusting the antenna, but I think the whole unit might just be old. I bought it at a garage sale a few years ago from this guy who was moving to Florida. He had all this fishing gear out too, like rods and tackle boxes. I’ve never really been into fishing, honestly. My uncle used to go ice fishing up in Michigan, and he’d sit out there in a little tent on the frozen lake for hours. I hate being cold. That’s why I always keep a spare blanket in the cab of my truck, just in case the heater goes out again. Last winter, the blower motor died right in the middle of a snowstorm, and I had to wear two pairs of gloves just to hold the steering wheel.
Do you often find yourself wondering if someone is hiding something from you?

Hiding something? I mean, I guess I don't really sit around wondering about it all the time. But people do keep things to themselves. Like my neighbor down the hall, Mrs. Gable. She's always so quiet when she brings her groceries in, but I know she's got a cat in there, even though the building has a strict no-pets policy. I saw a bag of Purina peeking out of her tote bag last week. I didn't say anything, though. I mean, why would I? It's not my business. 

I used to have a cat when I was a kid. His name was Barnaby, and he was this big orange tabby. He used to sleep right on top of my head at night, which was kind of annoying but also really sweet. He lived to be like, eighteen years old. We buried him in the backyard under the big oak tree. That tree was huge, it had to be at least a hundred years old. My brother built a treehouse in it one summer. He used all this scrap wood he found behind the hardware store. It was pretty rickety, honestly. We weren't allowed to go up there when it rained because the roof leaked so bad. I think the new owners of the house tore it down. It's a shame, really. But I guess people don't really want old, rickety treehouses in their yards anymore. They want those nice, plastic playsets with the swings and the slide. Have you seen those? They look so bright and colorful, but I feel like the plastic would get really hot in the summer sun.
Do you think most people have ulterior motives?

Ulterior motives? I don't know, maybe? I guess I haven't really thought about it like that. I mean, some people probably do, but I don't think everyone is walking around with some secret plan. Although, you know, my old supervisor at the warehouse definitely did. He was always scheduling me for the absolute worst shifts, the ones where you have to do inventory all night. 

Inventory is the worst. You just stand there with the scanner, beep, beep, beep, for hours. My hand used to cramp up so bad. I actually bought this special wrist brace from the pharmacy, the one with the metal splint in it? It helped a little, but it smelled weird after a while. Like, sort of like old rubber and sweat. I tried washing it in the sink with dish soap, but it just took forever to dry. I ended up leaving it on the radiator in my apartment, and it kind of melted the edge of the velcro. My apartment has those really old cast iron radiators that hiss and clank all night. Sometimes it sounds like someone is taking a hammer to the pipes down in the basement. The landlord says it's normal, but he doesn't live there. He lives out in the suburbs in this big house with a wrap-around porch. I saw a picture of it once when I went to drop off my rent check. He had all these hanging ferns on the porch, which I always think look so nice, but I can never keep plants alive. I bought a succulent once because they said you can't kill it, but I totally did. I think I watered it too much.
Do you often doubt the honesty of people you interact with?

Honesty? Um, I don't really doubt everyone's honesty, I guess. I mean, I don't sit around thinking everyone is lying to me all the time. But people do stretch the truth, don't they? Like when you ask someone how they are and they just say "fine" even if they're not. 

Like the cashier at the grocery store down the street. She always says she's fine, but she looks so tired. She has these really dark circles under her eyes. I bought this under-eye concealer once that was supposed to cover those up. It was in this little glass pot, and it was so expensive. I got it at that big makeup store in the mall. The mall used to be so busy when I was in high school, but now half the stores are empty. There used to be this great pretzel place right in the middle, near the fountain. They made these cinnamon sugar pretzels that were just amazing. I tried making pretzels at home once, but the dough didn't rise right. I think my yeast was expired. I always forget to check the expiration dates on baking stuff. I have a can of baking powder in my cupboard that's probably from like, 2018. I should probably throw it out, but I hate wasting things. My mom was always really strict about not wasting food. If we didn't finish our dinner, it went right into Tupperware for the next day. We had so much Tupperware, but the lids never matched the bottoms. It was like a puzzle every time you wanted to put leftovers away.
Do you generally assume that people are trying to take advantage of you?

Take advantage of me? No, I don't think so. I mean, I don't walk around thinking everyone is out to get me or use me. I just do my job, you know? I drive the paratransit van for the county, so mostly I just help people get to their doctor's appointments and stuff. 

Some of the regulars are really sweet. There's this one older gentleman, Mr. Henderson, who always gives me a butterscotch candy when I drop him off at dialysis. I don't really like butterscotch, honestly, it gets stuck in my teeth. I had a cavity filled last year and the dentist said I need to floss more. I bought those little plastic flosser things, the ones with the mint flavor? But I keep forgetting to use them. They're just sitting in my medicine cabinet next to this bottle of rubbing alcohol. I don't even know why I have so much rubbing alcohol. I think I bought a three-pack at Costco once because it was on sale. Costco is so overwhelming, though. The ceilings are so high and the lights buzz. I went there with my roommate last month to get paper towels, and we ended up buying a giant box of frozen taquitos. We ate them for dinner for like a week straight. My stomach felt so weird after that. I tried drinking ginger ale to settle it, but it went flat because I left the cap loose. I always do that. My dad used to get so mad at me for leaving the soda caps loose when I was a teenager. He'd say I was letting all the money fizz right out of the bottle.
Do you often find yourself questioning the intentions of those around you?

Questioning their intentions? Um, no, not really. I don't really think about what other people are planning to do, you know? I just kind of focus on what I need to get done for the day. Like, making sure I have enough gas in the van before my first pickup. 

The gas station on the corner near the depot has this really annoying pump, though. The handle doesn't lock, so you have to just stand there holding it the whole time. In the winter, your hand gets absolutely freezing. I lost one of my good winter gloves there last year. They were those nice leather ones with the cashmere lining. My sister got them for me for Christmas. She's always buying me really nice things that I end up ruining or losing. She works in marketing, so she makes a lot more money than I do. She just bought a new car, actually. A little blue hatchback. It has that new car smell, which I always think smells kind of like chemicals, but she loves it. She got these custom floor mats for it, too. They have her initials embroidered on them in silver thread. I tried to learn embroidery once, during the pandemic when everyone was doing crafts. I got one of those starter kits online, but the needle was so tiny I kept pricking my finger. I ended up just putting it in a drawer with all these old batteries and takeout menus. I should probably throw those menus away, since you can just look everything up on your phone now. But I kind of like looking at the pictures of the food. Especially the Chinese place down the street, they have pictures of all the combination platters.
Do you still believe that dispatch and other drivers are reporting on you and trying to interfere with your work?

Yeah, I mean, I know what's going on. I'm here because dispatch and compliance, they've been tracking my route changes through the computer system. And they make these little comments on the radio, you know? Even when people say it’s just normal oversight, I can tell certain drivers are reporting on me. It's so obvious. 

They use that same radio system we got upgraded to last year. The new mics have these curly cords that always get tangled around the gear shift. I tried untangling it once while I was parked, and I accidentally spilled my coffee all over the center console. It was that hazelnut coffee from the gas station, the one with the broken pump. I had to use an entire roll of paper towels to clean it up. The paper towels were the cheap kind, too, so they just kind of smeared the coffee around instead of absorbing it. I ended up buying one of those little pine tree air fresheners to cover up the smell, the "New Car" scent one. It didn't smell like a new car at all, it smelled like laundry detergent. I use the lavender laundry pods at home. They come in this big plastic tub that I always think I can reuse for something, but I never do. I just have like four empty tubs sitting in my laundry room. My sister told me I should use them to organize my shoes, but my shoes don't really fit in them. I wear a size 9, and I have these big clunky work boots that I have to wear for driving. They have steel toes, which is good because I dropped a wrench on my foot once when I was trying to fix a leaky pipe under my sink. I ended up having to call a plumber anyway. He charged me like two hundred dollars just to tighten a bolt. Plumbers make so much money. I wonder if I should have gone to trade school instead of getting my associate's degree.
Do you often have thoughts like the ones about dispatch and the drivers when you're not at work?

Thoughts about dispatch when I'm not at work? Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, when I'm home, I'm just home. I try to leave work at work, you know? Once I clock out, I just want to relax and watch TV. 

I've been watching this baking show on Netflix lately. It's the one where they have to make these crazy elaborate cakes that look like everyday objects. Like, someone made a cake that looked exactly like a pair of sneakers. It was wild. I don't bake, though. My oven is kind of broken. The temperature dial is all messed up, so if you set it to 350, it actually heats up to like 425. I burned a frozen pizza in there last month. It was one of those fancy ones with the cauliflower crust? It cost like nine dollars, and it just turned into a black hockey puck. I was so mad. I ended up just eating a bowl of cereal for dinner. I like that cereal with the little marshmallows in it. They get all soggy in the milk, which I know some people hate, but I kind of like it. I buy the generic brand in the huge bags, it's way cheaper than the boxes. The bags are annoying to close, though. I use those chip clips, but they always snap. I bought a pack of wooden clothespins to use instead, but my roommate took them all to hang up her polaroid pictures on this string of fairy lights she put up in the living room. The lights are pretty, I guess, but one of the bulbs is flickering and it drives me crazy. I told her we should replace it, but she said she likes the aesthetic. I don't really get what aesthetic she's going for, honestly.
Do you generally think that most people are out to take advantage of you in some way?

Take advantage of me? No, I don't... I don't really think people are trying to do that. I mean, most people are just trying to get by, right? Like, you just go to the store, pay for your stuff, and leave. 

I was at the grocery store yesterday, actually, getting more of that cereal. The lines were so long because they only had two registers open. It's always like that on Sunday afternoons. I usually try to go on Tuesday mornings when it's empty, but I had to pick up an extra shift this week. The cashier was this high school kid who looked like he was about to fall asleep standing up. He double-scanned my apples, but I caught it. Honeycrisp apples are way too expensive to pay for twice. They're like three dollars a pound right now. I remember when you could get a whole bag of apples for three dollars. My grandma used to make apple butter in this huge slow cooker she had. It would cook for like two days straight, and the whole house would smell amazing. She lived in this old farmhouse that had a wrap-around porch. We used to sit out there on this wooden swing she had. The chains on the swing were really rusty, and they would squeak every time you moved. I tried to oil them once with some WD-40, but the spray nozzle was clogged or something and it just kind of sputtered everywhere. It got all over my favorite jeans, the ones with the hole in the left knee. I still wear them, though, because they're the only ones that fit perfectly over my work boots.
Do you usually assume that strangers are trying to deceive you?

Deceive me? Like strangers? Um, no, I don't really assume that. Strangers are just strangers, you know? Like people you pass on the street. You don't really interact with them enough for them to trick you or anything. 

I was walking down by the river walk the other day, and there were so many people out because the weather was finally nice. It had been raining for like three days straight before that. My apartment gets really drafty when it rains, especially around the window in the kitchen. I tried to seal it with that plastic film you use a hairdryer on, but the hairdryer I have is really old and it overheats if you run it for more than five minutes. It just shuts off completely. I bought it at a thrift store when I first moved out of my parents' house. The thrift store is actually right next to this amazing taco truck. They make these al pastor tacos with pineapple on them, which I know sounds weird, but it's so good. I always get extra salsa verde, but they put it in those tiny little plastic cups with the lids that never snap on right. I spilled salsa all over my passenger seat last week trying to open one while I was at a stoplight. I had to use this upholstery cleaner I found in the trunk, but it left this weird water ring on the fabric. It kind of looks like a map of Australia now if you squint at it. I've always wanted to go to Australia, actually, to see the kangaroos. I saw a documentary about them once, and apparently they can't walk backwards. It's because of how their tails and legs are structured. It's kind of sad, really, just always having to move forward.
Do you often find yourself distrusting people you've just met?

Distrusting people? Um, no, not really. I mean, if I just met someone, I don't really have a reason to not trust them, right? They're just a new person. I usually just say hi and that's it. 

Like, there was this new guy who started at work last week. He's a dispatcher for the night shift, I think. He introduced himself in the breakroom when I was making coffee. The coffee machine we have there is one of those Keurig ones, but it's super loud. It sounds like an airplane taking off every time it brews. And the water reservoir is always empty, which is so annoying because the sink is all the way on the other side of the room. I brought in my own mug from home so I wouldn't have to use the styrofoam cups. It's a mug my sister got me for my birthday, it has a picture of a cat wearing sunglasses on it. It says "Too Cool for School." My sister has three cats, actually. Two of them are orange tabbies, and they are always getting into trouble. One of them, I think his name is Marmalade, knocked over a huge fern she had in her living room. Dirt went everywhere, all over her rug. She has this really nice Persian rug that she got at an estate sale. She's always going to estate sales on the weekends. I went with her once, but it was just a lot of old dusty furniture and creepy porcelain dolls. I don't like those dolls, their eyes always look like they're following you around the room. I saw a movie about a haunted doll once, and I couldn't sleep for a week. I had to leave the hallway light on, but the switch is kind of faulty, so you have to jiggle it to get it to stay on.
Do you often feel like people are watching you or talking about you behind your back?

Watching me? Well, yeah, I'm actually here because dispatch and compliance have been tracking my route changes through the computer system. They leave these little comments on the radio, too. Everyone says it's just normal oversight, but I can tell certain drivers are reporting on me, talking behind my back. 

The radio in my truck has been acting weird lately, anyway. It gets this awful static right around 2:00 PM every day. It sounds like someone crinkling aluminum foil right next to your ear. I tried to listen to a podcast instead, one about deep-sea diving. Did you know there are fish down there that have their own built-in flashlights? It's called bioluminescence. They use it to attract prey because it's completely pitch black down there. I went swimming in the ocean once when I was a kid, on a family trip to Florida. The water was so warm, like bathwater. But I stepped on a jellyfish and it stung my foot. It swelled up like a balloon and we had to go to this little clinic near the beach. The waiting room had all these posters about sun safety, and the air conditioning was blasting so high I was shivering. My dad bought me a snow cone afterward to make me feel better. It was cherry flavored, but it melted really fast in the heat and got all over my hands. They were stained red for two days. I tried scrubbing them with that orange pumice soap mechanics use, but it just made my skin really dry. I had to buy this special lotion with shea butter in it. It smelled like coconuts, which always reminds me of sunscreen and summer. I love summer, except for the mosquitoes. They always seem to bite me more than anyone else.
Do you feel like people are watching you or talking about you behind your back even when you're not at work?

Not at work? Um, no, I don't really notice anything like that when I'm not working. I mean, when I'm off the clock, I mostly just keep to myself, you know? Go to the grocery store, run errands, that kind of thing. 

I was at the grocery store yesterday, actually, in the produce section. They had these huge watermelons on sale, the seedless kind. I love watermelon, but it's such a hassle to cut up. You need a really big knife, and the one I have is kind of dull. I tried to sharpen it with one of those little handheld sharpeners, but I think I did it at the wrong angle because it just made it worse. I ended up having to use a serrated bread knife to cut the watermelon, which made a huge mess. Juice got all over the counter and dripped down the front of the cabinets. The cabinets in my apartment are this really ugly oak color from the 90s. I asked my landlord if I could paint them white to brighten up the kitchen, but he said no. He's really strict about modifying the apartment. He won't even let me put nails in the wall to hang pictures. I have to use those Command strips, but they always fall down if it gets too humid. I tried to hang a picture of my dog, Buster, and it fell right in the middle of the night. Scared me half to death. I thought someone was breaking in. Buster is a golden retriever mix, he's so sweet. He loves to chase tennis balls, but he always chews the fuzz off them until they're just bald rubber. I have to buy them in bulk from the sporting goods store. The guy who works there always wears these bright neon yellow shoelaces. They're so bright they almost glow in the dark. I wonder where he buys them.
Do you still believe that people are plotting against you?

Well, yeah, like I was just saying a minute ago, that's exactly what's happening at work. Dispatch and compliance are definitely plotting, tracking all my route changes through the computer system. And the other drivers are reporting on me with those little comments on the radio. Everyone keeps telling me it's just normal oversight, but I know what they're doing. 

The computer system in those trucks is a nightmare anyway, to be honest. The screen glare is so bad when you're driving at night. I had to buy these special yellow-tinted glasses just so I wouldn't get a headache from staring at it. I ordered them online, but the shipping got totally messed up. The tracking said the package went to Ohio for some reason, which makes zero sense. My aunt lives in Ohio, though, near Cleveland. She makes these amazing snickerdoodle cookies every Christmas and mails them to me in these little decorative tins. Last year, the tin had a picture of ice skaters on it, but one of the skaters looked exactly like my old high school gym teacher. He used to make us run the mile on the track every single Friday, even if it was raining. I ruined my favorite pair of sneakers in the mud once. They were these bright blue high-tops. I tried putting them in the dryer to fix them, but they just thumped around so loud it sounded like the machine was going to explode. I had to turn the TV all the way up just to hear my show.

Like I was just saying, dispatch and compliance are tracking my route changes through the computer system specifically to mess with me. And the other drivers are definitely reporting on me to them, I know they are. I hear those little comments on the radio. It’s totally on purpose to ruin my routes. 

Which, honestly, my routes are hard enough right now because of all the construction on the interstate. I swear they’ve been fixing that same stretch of highway since 2019. The orange cones are just everywhere. I actually ran over one of those cones a few years ago when I was driving a smaller rig.
